evals.prompt: I want a reusable JavaFX component that I can use directly as a tag in parent FXML, like <SearchBar queryText="abc"/>. Show me: (1) parent FXML imports + tag usage, (2) component FXML using fx:root, (3) Java component class with the right FXMLLoader wiring and queryText attribute mapping.
evals.expected_output: Shows custom component as FXML class tag with import lines, fx:root-backed component class, correct setRoot/setController/load order, and queryText setter/property mapping.
expectations: Includes parent FXML import processing instruction(s) and direct custom tag usage
Uses fx:root in component FXML and avoids fx:controller conflict for the same document
Java component class shows setRoot(this) and setController(this) before loader.load()
Explains how queryText attribute maps to writable bean API (setter/property)

evals.prompt: In my parent FXML I use custom tags like <PrayerRowComponent prayerName="Fajr" prayerTime="04:50 AM" prayerValue="04:50 AM"/>. Explain exactly what APIs the component class must expose so these attributes work, and show a concise component class snippet with these properties.
evals.expected_output: Explains attribute-to-setter/property mapping for custom tag usage and provides matching component APIs for prayerName/prayerTime/prayerValue.
expectations: Explicitly maps prayerName/prayerTime/prayerValue tag attributes to writable component APIs
Shows concrete setter/property methods for each attribute
Explains JavaBean mapping rule (fooBar -> setFooBar) and minimum required public API

evals.prompt: My parent FXML has <HomeComponent/> and <MainScreenHeader/> tags, but loader fails with class/property errors. Give me a step-by-step troubleshooting checklist focused on custom class tags (imports, class visibility, constructor/wiring, attribute mapping), plus Scene Builder notes. Also clarify when SceneBuilder.cfg classpath hack is appropriate.
evals.expected_output: Provides tag-focused checklist (imports/class tags, fx:root constructor wiring, attribute mapping), root causes, and last-resort framing for SceneBuilder.cfg after modern workflows.
expectations: Provides a numbered, step-by-step troubleshooting checklist focused on custom class tags
Includes a distinct likely-root-causes section covering import/class resolution and cannot-set-property issues
States that SceneBuilder.cfg classpath hack is a last-resort legacy fallback

evals.prompt: I need to build a home screen for my app that shows: a greeting message, daily hadith card, prayer times with notifications, and a favorites section. Create the FXML and Java components for this screen.
evals.expected_output: Multiple small, focused component files (not one monolithic FXML). Each component under 60 lines. Clear composition pattern in parent screen component. Explanation of why each component was extracted.
expectations: Creates 5+ separate component FXML files (not one large file)
Each component FXML is under 60 lines (excluding imports)
Parent/screen component only handles layout, uses child component tags
Explains component boundaries and decomposition rationale
Each component class has correct fx:root wiring (setRoot/setController/load)
Components expose clear attribute APIs (setters/properties)

evals.prompt: I have a 200-line FXML file with a greeting section, hadith section, prayer times section, and favorites section all in one file. How should I refactor this? Show me the decomposition strategy and the resulting component structure.
evals.expected_output: Step-by-step decomposition strategy showing how to extract each section into its own component. Results in 4+ small component files plus one parent composition file. Explains the decomposition process and benefits.
expectations: Identifies logical boundaries in the monolithic FXML
Shows how to extract each section into a separate component
Resulting components are each under 60 lines
Parent file only handles layout composition
Explains decomposition strategy and benefits (reusability, testability, maintainability)
Provides concrete before/after FXML examples

evals.prompt: Create a PrayerRowComponent that I can reuse 5 times in a GridPane for different prayers (Fajr, Dhuhr, Asr, Maghrib, Isha). Each row should show prayer name, time, and a notification toggle. Show the component FXML, Java class, and how to use it 5 times in parent FXML.
evals.expected_output: Single focused PrayerRowComponent (under 40 lines FXML) with prayerName/prayerTime attribute APIs. Parent FXML shows 5 instances of the component with different attribute values. Component class exposes proper setters/properties.
expectations: PrayerRowComponent FXML is under 40 lines and focused on single responsibility
Component class exposes setPrayerName/setPrayerTime setters with property APIs
Parent FXML uses component 5 times with different attribute values
Demonstrates DRY principle - no duplicated markup
Component uses fx:root with correct wiring pattern

evals.prompt: What are the signs that tell me I should extract a separate FXML component? Give me concrete criteria and examples of when to decompose vs when to keep things inline.
evals.expected_output: Clear decomposition criteria with examples: logical grouping, reusability potential, complexity threshold (15+ lines, 5+ nesting), independent state, visual boundaries. Shows good vs bad examples.
expectations: Lists specific decomposition criteria (logical grouping, reusability, complexity, state, visual boundaries)
Provides concrete size limits (20-40 lines target, 60 max, 5 nesting levels)
Shows good decomposition example with multiple small components
Shows bad monolith example with everything inline
Explains when NOT to decompose (simple, one-off UI with 5-10 lines)
